evals.prompt: I just joined this team and I need to add a 'last login' field to the user profile page. I've never seen this codebase before — it's a Node.js app, there's a src/ folder with controllers, services, and models directories. Where do I even start?
evals.expected_output: Claude reads the codebase, produces a Mermaid diagram of the layered architecture, presents it, then asks the engineer ONE question to start the interrogation — not a list of questions.
expectations: Claude produces a Mermaid diagram before asking any interrogation questions
After presenting the diagram, Claude asks exactly one question (not a list)
Claude does not ask the engineer to explain the codebase before reading it themselves
The diagram uses flowchart TD or flowchart LR syntax
Claude presents the diagram and invites the engineer to walk through it before interrogating

evals.prompt: I'm onboarding at a new company. The codebase is a Python Django monolith with separate apps for 'accounts', 'orders', and 'payments'. My first ticket is to add an email notification when an order ships. I don't know how this system works yet.
evals.expected_output: Claude explores the Django app structure, maps the dependency direction between apps, produces a diagram, then interrogates one question at a time. Does not dump a list of questions.
expectations: Claude produces a Mermaid diagram showing the Django apps and their relationships
Claude asks one question after presenting the diagram, not multiple
The interrogation probes WHY the system is shaped the way it is, not just WHAT it does
Claude does not move to orient or pseudocode before the exit condition is met

evals.prompt: can you explain how this is structured? it's a microservices setup, there's an api-gateway, auth-service, user-service, and notification-service. I need to add rate limiting but I'm not sure where it goes.
evals.expected_output: Claude reads the services, produces a service-to-service flowchart LR diagram, then interrogates the engineer on ownership and boundaries one question at a time.
expectations: Claude produces a flowchart LR diagram for the microservices
Claude asks one question to begin interrogation, not a bulleted list
At least one interrogation question probes ownership or boundary responsibility
Claude does not suggest where rate limiting goes before the engineer has demonstrated architectural understanding
